page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Eadsv7 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores, running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 1890 GB NVMe SSD.

In benchmark evaluations, the E32-8ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng single-core score and high single-threaded compression and decompression throughput. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average tier. The system achieves strong performance in text generation for small-scale language models, though prompt processing for medium-scale models is relatively weak.

Given the high memory density of 32.0 GB per vCPU paired with local NVMe storage, this instance offers high resource density for memory-bound applications without the overhead of scaling up vCPU counts. It is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, caching layers like Redis, and memory-heavy data processing tasks that benefit from fast local temporary storage and strong single-core execution.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8ads_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance from the Eadsv7 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, alongside 256.0 GB of RAM and a local 1890 GB NVMe SSD. The hardware configuration delivers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmarks highlight top-tier single-core CPU execution and single-threaded data compression, alongside average multi-core and memory bandwidth performance. Lacking a dedicated GPU, it relies on its high-frequency AMD EPYC processor for compute tasks. This server is designed for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, caching layers, and applications requiring substantial memory capacity relative to compute resources.
